inputs.quote: Source: Sequencing of 19 whole genomes detected 25 mutations that were fixed in the 40,000 generations of the experiment. NATURE, 2009

inputs.name: G_f 1,600 (2025 paper)
inputs.quote: Sequencing detected 25 mutations that were fixed over approximately 40,000 bacterial generations, yielding an average of 1,600 generations per fixed mutation.

inputs.name: citation of the 1,600 datum in the 2025 papers

inputs.name: Barrick et al. 2009 genome span
inputs.quote: Although adaptation decelerated sharply, genomic evolution was nearly constant for 20,000 generations.

inputs.name: G_f 1,322 (non-mutators, 60,000 gens, mean 45.4 fixations)
inputs.quote: The average across all five non-mutator populations at 60,000 generations is 45.4 fixations, yielding a cumulative rate of 1,322 generations per fixation.

inputs.name: G_f 893 (clone pair, 50,000 gens)
inputs.quote: cross- validated at 893 generations per fixation by clone-pair analysis at 50,000 generations.

inputs.name: G_f 1,400 (2nd-edition abstract)
inputs.quote: we calculate that natural selection can accomplish at most 180 fixations on the human lineage given 252,000 generations and 1,400 generations per fixation (the fastest empirical rate ever measured in any organism). This represents 0.000088% of the approximately 205 million fixations required on the human lineage. The shortfall is 1,139,000-fold.

inputs.name: G_f 1,587 (strict count)
inputs.quote: go to the high-resolution data set for all 273,000 generations across the 12 populations, then run the numbers, is 1,587 generations per fixation.
inputs.locator: Q85, AI Central An Intelligent Groove ¶16 (2026-10-03)
